key_insight: This paper systematically re-checks which loss functions actually help deep regression on tabular data, instead of assuming Mean Squared Error is always the best default. It also shows that the widely used practice of global early stopping has important limits that can distort comparisons across objectives.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the lack of a fair, apples-to-apples comparison of regression objectives for tabular deep learning. Prior results were hard to trust because studies used different datasets, backbones, and evaluation protocols.
method: Re-evaluate multiple regression objectives under a controlled, standardized benchmark setup.
Compare objectives across the same datasets, model backbones, and training/evaluation protocol.
Analyze the interaction between objective choice and global early stopping to isolate its effect on reported performance.
impact: For practitioners, this helps identify when switching away from MSE is worthwhile and when it is not. It also encourages more reliable benchmarking, reducing the risk of overestimating gains from new regression losses.
visual_elements: A side-by-side benchmark table comparing regression objectives
A flow diagram showing the evaluation pipeline and standardized protocol
A line chart illustrating training curves and early stopping behavior
An icon-based comparison of objectives vs. MSE on key metrics
paper_title: Revisiting Tabular Deep Regression: Objectives and the Limits of Global Early Stopping
paper_authors: Danil Rudenko, Georgii Bulgakov, Nikolay Kartashev, Ivan Rubachev, Daniil Krasylnikov
